ai.definition: Multi-Material Jetting is an additive manufacturing process that allows for the simultaneous deposition and curing of multiple materials with varying properties such as hardness and color.
ai.howItWorks: The technology uses inkjet-style heads to deposit different polymers or resins, which are then instantly cured using UV light. This enables the creation of objects with complex internal structures and varied material properties in a single print run.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional additive manufacturing processes often struggle with printing multiple materials simultaneously, leading to limitations in the complexity and functionality of printed parts.
ai.manufacturing: The process involves precise control over the deposition rate and curing conditions for each material being used. This requires advanced calibration and software capabilities to ensure accurate layer-by-layer formation.
ai.buildProcess: A multi-material jetting system typically consists of multiple inkjet heads, each containing a different material. The printer deposits these materials in layers, which are then cured using UV light or another curing method.
ai.costDrivers: Costs can be driven by the quality and variety of materials used, as well as the complexity of the printing process and the need for specialized equipment.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to see increased adoption in prototyping and tooling applications due to its ability to produce parts with complex material properties.
ai.regulation: Current regulations are largely focused on safety standards for the materials used, as well as environmental considerations during manufacturing and disposal of printed objects.
ai.risks: Potential risks include material compatibility issues, curing inconsistencies, and the need for precise control over the printing process to ensure part quality.
ai.profitability: Profitability is influenced by the ability to produce complex prototypes or tools that reduce time-to-market and improve product development efficiency. However, costs associated with materials and equipment can be high.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may focus on expanding material options, improving print speed and resolution, and reducing manufacturing energy intensity.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking.

glossary.def: Precision nozzles that deposit materials in a controlled manner, similar to inkjet printers.
A process where UV light is used to rapidly cure or solidify the deposited materials.

subsystems.name: Printhead array
subsystems.role: jets droplets of multiple photopolymer materials and a support material onto the build area.
parts: nozzle plates with dozens to hundreds of orifices

subsystems.name: Material delivery
subsystems.role: supplies and conditions the liquid resins so they jet reliably.

subsystems.name: UV curing system
subsystems.role: solidifies each deposited layer instantly as the printhead passes.

subsystems.name: Motion and build stage
subsystems.role: moves the printhead across the build area and lowers the platform for each new layer.

subsystems.name: Support removal system
subsystems.role: removes the gel-like or soluble support material that holds overhangs and internal voids.

subsystems.name: Control software
subsystems.role: slices the 3D model, assigns materials and colors to each voxel, and coordinates jetting and curing.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the digital model
buildSteps.detail: The part is designed in CAD and then sliced into layers of typically 14–30 micrometres. Each voxel is assigned a material, hardness or color, so the software knows which printhead to fire at every point.

buildSteps.title: Load materials
buildSteps.detail: Cartridges of photocurable resin — sometimes several rigid and flexible grades plus a support material — are loaded into the machine. The system primes and purges the printheads.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the printheads
buildSteps.detail: The machine runs a test pattern to align the multiple printheads and verify droplet size and placement. Poor calibration would cause gaps or material mixing between layers.

buildSteps.title: Print layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: The printhead carriage scans across the build platform, jetting microscopic droplets of build and support materials. A UV lamp mounted beside the heads cures the droplets immediately, forming a solid layer.

buildSteps.title: Lower and repeat
buildSteps.detail: The build platform drops by one layer thickness, and the carriage scans again. This repeats until the object is complete, with support material deposited wherever overhangs or internal channels need it.

buildSteps.title: Remove the part
buildSteps.detail: The finished part is lifted from the platform. Excess uncured resin is wiped or blown away.

buildSteps.title: Strip the support
buildSteps.detail: The part is placed in a water jet or solvent bath to dissolve or blast away the support material, leaving the multi-material geometry intact.

buildSteps.title: Post-process
buildSteps.detail: Optional steps include additional UV curing for full strength, sanding, polishing, or painting. Some materials can be machined or drilled after printing.

pathway.milestone: commercial machines print parts with dozens of materials and full-color gradients for prototypes, dental models, jigs and fixtures
pathway.unlocks: fast iteration on realistic multi-material prototypes and custom tooling.

pathway.milestone: higher-throughput printheads and larger build envelopes
pathway.unlocks: printing bigger parts and small production batches directly.

pathway.milestone: new engineering photopolymers that mimic thermoplastics, elastomers and biocompatible resins
pathway.unlocks: functional end-use parts for medical devices, wearables and fluidics.

pathway.milestone: automated support removal and integrated post-processing
pathway.unlocks: unattended, factory-style production of multi-material jetted parts.
